purpose: Separate the reviewed current nodewerk implementation from proposed semantic families and optional backends, while preserving the complete Werkkzeug reference catalogue.
scope_notes: This is a family-level planning map, not an exhaustive operator-by-operator equivalence result or an engine feature implementation.

existing_operator_ids are IDs present in the reviewed registry/compiler; current_scope and limitations say whether their release realization exists, is restricted, or is only represented by schema/reference evaluation.
A fixed shader override, standalone experiment, registered schema or CPU image oracle is not counted as a reusable general-purpose implementation.
Current limits such as one mesh/material, four orbital camera keys or 64 audio events describe the pinned implementation. They do not establish permanent product limits or new acceptance gates.
Proposed semantics are behavior descriptions, not committed nw.* IDs, interface spellings or guarantees of adoption.
Candidate backends are planning options, not approved integrations. Technologies may support several families and one family may require several operators/passes.
Reference query terms and prospective names are retrieval hints only. Their appearances in individual source variants and graph uses must be linked to inventory records before claiming coverage.
This review makes no physical execution, image-equivalence, performance or complete-demo reproducibility claim.

policy.authoring_semantics: Backend-neutral authored functions; SDK/API/vendor names belong to capability-qualified lowering selection rather than artist-facing semantic node identities.
policy.common_fallback: Required semantics retain a common non-RTX implementation. Optional lowerings consume the same semantic graph; common and optional artifacts remain separately exportable.
policy.training_rule: No nodewerk-owned training, fine-tuning, data preparation for training, per-asset/per-production model fitting or runtime/online model training. Fixed externally pretrained inference may be evaluated.
policy.geometry: Polygon meshes, implicit fields and other justified representations may coexist. SDF/CSG is not a general replacement for topology, selections, UVs, skeletal authoring or every historical modeling operation.
policy.reference_preservation: Keep all inventoried reference records. Mark coverage and replacement relations without deleting historical entries or assuming that a technology replaces an entire family.
policy.clean_room: Use Farbrausch sources/data to document operator intent, metadata and requirements. Do not copy, mechanically translate or port their implementation into nodewerk.
policy.implementation_architecture: Extend the shared graph/compiler/export/PackagePlayer/Studio and temporal/audio systems. Do not create a fixture-specific second renderer or introduce a general runtime graph interpreter.
policy.prioritization: Order work by shared prerequisites and actual reachable production graphs. The priorities below are suggestions and add no new frozen contracts or validation gates.

current_capability.full: All explicitly described family semantics are realized by reviewed reusable implementations. No family is promoted to this state by this starter review.
current_capability.partial: A concrete bounded subset, restricted fixture or supporting implementation is present; stated limitations prevent a full-family claim.
current_capability.none: No reviewed reusable implementation or relevant realized fixture for this family was identified in the stated sources.

reference_mapping.unreviewed: Individual reference operator parameter domains, output contracts, temporal behavior and downstream graph uses have not been checked for equivalence.
reference_mapping.partial: Reserved for a future explicit mapping covering only a stated subset of reference operator behavior.
reference_mapping.full: Reserved for a future explicit mapping that preserves the required authored control and downstream semantics in a declared use.

current_state.implemented: Concrete reusable implementation exists for current_scope, without implying that the broad family is complete or every registered port is generally lowerable.
current_state.restricted_fixture: Concrete output exists inside a constrained exporter/fixed pipeline or dedicated shader fixture; it is not a general reusable family.
current_state.experimental: Concrete capability-qualified experimental implementation exists, without implying reusable authoring support or default adoption.
current_state.planned: A new semantic extension is planned; supporting schemas or narrower primitives may already exist and are listed separately.
current_state.deferred: No implementation is scheduled by this map; retain the requirement and reconsider after a real production demonstrates need.

reference_usage.rationale: Registration count and name matching cannot identify reachable operators in .k/.wz4 production graphs. Decode/reference graph roots and dependencies before prioritizing by actual use.
reference_usage.replacement_relations_note: Intentionally empty. A family-level candidate or similar output is not yet a verified one-to-one or many-to-many replacement relation.

priority_order.title: Connect a reusable production scene
priority_order.outcome: Multiple independently authored objects/materials and cameras flow through the shared exporter/player, with consistent scene identities and required image channels.

priority_order.title: Add construction required by selected scenes
priority_order.outcome: Choose mesh and field construction based on actual graph needs; prove combinations through shared operators instead of replacing a monolithic fixture shader.

priority_order.title: Connect spatial, temporal and audible effects
priority_order.outcome: Actual scene-dependent visibility/reflection, occluded spatial particles, image history, postprocessing and procedural sound compose into a continuous authored sequence.

priority_order.title: Evaluate optional enhancements and demand-led gaps
priority_order.outcome: Assess allowed pretrained inference and additional semantics only against concrete requirements; apply optional mesh/DXR/Work-Graphs optimizations after the corresponding shared semantic path exists.

locators: Initialization, advancement, loop reset, seek, and replay
Optional experiment targets and shared production runtime

sources.note: Planning evidence only. The issue body is not pinned by the repository revision and may subsequently change.

families.title: Scalar/vector control and shader expressions
current_scope: CPU reference evaluation implements the listed control/math values; the restricted ShaderExpr language composes expressions and lowers reachable shader roots to compute HLSL.
limitations: CPU graph evaluation and schema registration alone do not establish that arbitrary CPU values drive every release render parameter.
The ShaderExpr language is restricted; it is not unrestricted HLSL, a general material language or scripting.
proposed_semantics: Reuse typed math, seeds and curve controls in the expanded scene, material and effect semantics.

common: Compile-time folding and specialization; existing CPU control/reference path; conventional compute HLSL.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Procedural texture generation and combination
current_scope: The reviewed instanced exporter generates seeded multi-octave 2D value noise as a texture at initialization; CPU reference generation exists.
Noise dimensions, seed, octaves, scale, lacunarity and gain are authored parameters.
limitations: build_package permits one texture recipe and one generated texture in the fixed 3D pipeline.
A procedural recipe or upload schema does not prove a general reusable bitmap graph.
No full Werkkzeug bitmap/filter family has been mapped.
proposed_semantics: Composable noise, gradients, masks, color operations, coordinate transforms and texture combinations driven by selected production needs.

common: Compile-time or initialization compute; CPU evaluation where appropriate.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Image layers and scene/effect composition
current_scope: Fullscreen ShaderExpr rendering exists.
G-buffer/composite port schemas and CPU image-oracle evaluation exist; these are not evidence of a reusable heterogeneous scene/layer renderer.
limitations: The reviewed NW-06 package binds one rendered image to a prescribed bloom/tonemap chain.
The reviewed schemas do not expose the planned complete color/depth/camera-metadata composition interface.
proposed_semantics: Compose actual rendered scene color and effect layers with explicit alpha convention and depth compatibility.
Expose typed depth and camera metadata; add motion/normal/material channels when required by a selected effect.

common: Shared raster/compute passes within the existing resource scheduler.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Polygonal primitives and generated mesh recipes
current_scope: Torus generation has concrete CPU and initialization-compute implementations, including indices, normals and UVs.
The 3D exporter has a concrete indexed/instanced geometry path.
limitations: The reviewed exporter constructs TorusParameters even when accepting the generic mesh.recipe identity.
One mesh source is permitted by the fixed lowering; a vertices/indices recipe schema is not arbitrary mesh construction.
Mesh shaders do not supply missing modeling semantics.
proposed_semantics: Add the bounded polygonal primitives actually needed by productions; allow polygon meshes and implicit surfaces to coexist.
Use representation-appropriate construction without promising one-to-one historical topology.

common: CPU/initialization-compute generation and indexed rasterization.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Polygon selections and topology editing
current_scope: No dedicated selection, extrusion, subdivision, bevel or arbitrary topology-editing operator was found in the reviewed current registry.
limitations: Implicit CSG or smooth union does not generally preserve face/edge selection, topology, UV seams or subsequent mesh-edit behavior.
The NW-13 issue explicitly defers a general mesh-editing suite; a real production may motivate a bounded addition.
proposed_semantics: Retain explicit uncovered requirements for selections, extrusion, subdivision, bevel and topology-aware operations.
Select a small independent implementation only when a production demonstrates the need; do not count SDF resemblance as full coverage.

common: Future compiler-side/CPU or compute mesh processing, if selected.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: UVs, normals and surface/material attributes
current_scope: The torus generator writes analytic normals and UVs in its vertex layout; SceneVS carries them to the raster pixel stage.
limitations: There is no dedicated reusable UV authoring, seam editing, tangent generation or general normal-processing operator in the reviewed registry.
Automatically generated primitive attributes do not cover arbitrary UV surgery or stable selected-face material assignments.
proposed_semantics: Preserve required UV/normal/material attributes through mesh operations and conversions.
Add bounded attribute generation/transform operations when needed; keep advanced UV editing explicitly deferred.

common: Compiler-side or conventional compute processing; shared vertex/mesh data.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Implicit primitives, CSG and bounded surface evaluation
current_scope: NW-10 demonstrates a fixed sphere/torus smooth-union SDF scene through one intro shader supplied as generated_shaders_override.
The reviewed registry contains no reusable SDF or CSG operator IDs.
limitations: NW-10's fixed shader and fixed operator-set check are an executable fixture, not an authored composable SDF/CSG vocabulary.
No general replacement claim for polygon selections, extrusion, subdivision or UV editing follows from this fixture.
proposed_semantics: Bounded implicit sphere, box, cylinder/capsule and torus fields; union, intersection, subtraction and smooth union.
A shared realization boundary that preserves material identity and lets implicit and polygonal geometry coexist.

common: Bounded shader evaluation/raymarching or compute-generated geometry plus rasterization, selected for the workload.
optional: Capability-qualified mesh or DXR realization preserving the same authored semantic; not required for common correctness.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Deformation and procedural displacement
current_scope: SceneVS applies a sinusoidal, absolute-tick Y-axis twist to local vertices and normals, controlled by max_twist_degrees.
limitations: The existing twist is embedded in the single torus/instance render path, not an arbitrary chain of geometry modifiers.
No generic bend, noise displacement or selection-aware deformation operator was found in the reviewed registry.
proposed_semantics: Composable bounded transforms, bend, twist and seeded displacement for suitable representations.
Preserve representation-specific attributes and clarify which field/domain operations cover a historical modeling intent only partially.

common: Compiler specialization, conventional compute/vertex processing or bounded field evaluation.
optional: Mesh-shader evaluation where useful; ray-traced realization only after the deformed scene is represented consistently.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Repetition and procedural instancing
current_scope: A seeded instance recipe produces a bounded flat table of transforms and material indices for one generated mesh.
The reviewed schema bounds count to 4096; this is an existing implementation limit, not a proposed permanent product limit.
limitations: One instances recipe is selected by build_package.
The current path is not arbitrary heterogeneous scene construction or a general repetition graph.
proposed_semantics: Bounded Cartesian/axis repetition and procedural instancing with shared geometry and stable identities.
Keep field repetition, duplicated mesh construction and scene instancing distinct where their output semantics differ.

common: Initialization/compile-time generation and conventional instanced rasterization.
optional: Mesh shaders; Work Graphs only for a workload that benefits from GPU-created work.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Scene objects, identity and heterogeneous composition
current_scope: The current concrete 3D path renders one mesh/texture/material/light/camera set with flat instances.
scene.flat has a CPU table-like authoring value; its existence is not a general scene renderer.
limitations: build_package.unique_node rejects multiple mesh, material, camera, light, instance and render nodes in this lowering.
The reviewed path does not expose authored heterogeneous room, door, character and prop objects with independent material bindings.
proposed_semantics: Stable scene objects binding geometry/surface, material and transform; compose heterogeneous objects and light collections.
Share geometry and preserve object/material identity for primary visibility, shadows, reflections and temporal consumers.

common: Shared compiler/export specialization, generated tables and existing PackagePlayer raster/compute path.
optional: Optional mesh and DXR lowerings must consume the same semantic scene.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Rigid transforms and articulated part animation
current_scope: A matrix constant type, generated instance transforms and fixed analytic twist exist.
limitations: A matrix value in the registry does not establish authored transform tracks, hierarchy composition or independent object motion in the exported renderer.
The reviewed concrete 3D path does not implement a general parent-child rigid part authoring workflow.
proposed_semantics: Compose position/rotation/scale and bounded parent-child transforms with explicit pivots and interpolation.
Animate rigid linked parts, doors and attached props; a general skeletal editing/skinning suite remains outside this initial scope.

common: Compile-time/generated buffers and bounded CPU/compute evaluation in the shared player.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Time, curves, cues and action-time mapping
current_scope: Integer 48000-tick timing, rational frame stepping, scalar curves and event-cursor semantics are implemented in shared timeline tools.
History adds fixed-step replay/reset; procedural audio supplies an optional sample-clock boundary.
limitations: Existing scalar curves and event infrastructure do not by themselves provide the planned independently controlled action-time and camera-time authoring graph.
The reviewed renderer has a special four-key orbital camera path; it is not a general sequencer.
proposed_semantics: Typed tracks and explicit mapping from authoritative presentation/audio ticks to action time.
Freeze, reverse and resume with declared independent camera and one-shot cue policies; propagate time discontinuities to stateful effects.

common: Shared timeline/audio clock, compiled schedules and bounded reconstruction.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Camera pose, paths and shots
current_scope: Projection parameters and a scalar orbital-angle curve are exposed.
_parse_camera_keys accepts at most four keys; the reviewed SceneVS computes an eye on a fixed-height orbit looking at the origin.
limitations: Projection schemas are not general camera position/orientation tracks.
The current concrete path lacks independently authored camera poses, target/up tracks and shot-cut sequencing.
proposed_semantics: Authored camera position and orientation or target/up, projection, bounded keyframes and explicit shot cuts.
Publish camera discontinuities and allow camera motion while action time is frozen.

common: Shared CPU/compute curve evaluation and ordinary view/projection transforms.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Material description and effective surface shading
current_scope: The concrete raster shader reads base color, roughness, metallic and specular plus one procedural albedo texture; these parameters affect its analytic shading.
limitations: This is a single-material fixed path, not a complete material graph or a general physically based BSDF implementation.
The common ScenePS output is opaque; the reviewed family has no authored emission/local-light contribution model or complete secondary-hit material lookup.
proposed_semantics: Multiple effective material identities, authored color/roughness/metallic/specular/emission and required procedural texture bindings.
Preserve the same material identity during mesh/implicit evaluation and primary/secondary visibility; declare whether emission contributes to illumination.

common: Shared raster/compute shading and compiler specialization.
optional: Material-aware DXR hit shading; externally pretrained inference only if a concrete allowed use case warrants it.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Light sources and direct illumination
current_scope: One directional-light record supplies direction/color to the concrete raster scene shader.
limitations: The fixed exporter selects a single light.
No dedicated point/spot light operator or heterogeneous light collection was found in the reviewed registry; the shader's ambient constant is not scene-derived indirect illumination.
proposed_semantics: Bounded light collections, point/spot lights and authored intensity, color, falloff and range.
Keep visible emissive surfaces and illumination contribution explicit.

common: Conventional raster/compute direct lighting.
optional: DXR visibility; sampling approaches such as RTXDI only after shared scene/light/material inputs exist and a concrete workload is selected.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Primary visibility and shared rendering realization
current_scope: The common path provides indexed/instanced raster rendering and fullscreen compute-image presentation.
NW-11 provides separate mesh-shader experiment targets using generated geometry and the shared runtime.
limitations: The reviewed 3D lowering is fixed around a single resource set.
A successful experiment target does not by itself add a general mesh-shader authoring operator or prove default adoption.
proposed_semantics: Render the expanded semantic scene through one shared compiler/resource/player architecture.
Preserve authored geometry/material/camera identity across common and optional realizations.

common: Existing D3D12 raster/compute path; bounded field realization where selected.
optional: Capability-qualified mesh-shader realization; other optional backends selected per actual workload.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Scene-dependent shadow visibility
current_scope: The reviewed common ScenePS evaluates direct analytic lighting without a scene shadow query.
The existing NW-11 ray-query fixture is a bounded reflected-surface experiment, not a reusable shadow semantic.
limitations: No public shadow operator was found in the reviewed registry.
A modern shadow algorithm can replace a historical implementation only while preserving required authored control and scene dependence.
proposed_semantics: Bounded shadow visibility against the same current scene and transforms as primary visibility.
Choose a suitable common implementation and an optional DXR/ray-query implementation with declared behavior.

common: A workload-appropriate non-DXR implementation, such as shadow mapping or bounded analytic/field visibility.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Scene reflection and environment response
current_scope: NW-11 TraceReflectedSurface performs a real inline ray query and returns a hit boolean.
ReflectionRadiance maps hits to a fixed color and misses to an analytic environment; the experiment is integrated with shared generated scene resources.
limitations: The fixture does not resolve the actual hit object's material/radiance or provide a reusable authored reflection operator.
Its deliberately bounded reflected segment is not a general one-bounce scene reflection implementation.
proposed_semantics: One-bounce material-aware reflected radiance from the nearest valid hit, with explicit environment/miss and roughness behavior.
Retain environment authoring even when ray tracing replaces an approximation for reflected geometry.

common: A suitable bounded common non-DXR reflection realization with declared limitations/tolerances.
optional: DXR/inline ray queries against the shared scene.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Ambient occlusion and indirect illumination
current_scope: No reusable scene AO or GI operator was found in the reviewed current registry.
The reviewed raster shader includes a constant ambient term; this is not geometric AO or indirect illumination.
limitations: AO and GI are different authored/rendering semantics and cannot be marked mutually interchangeable from similar darkening.
NW-13 makes secondary visibility/AO conditional on a production need; general GI is not an implemented baseline.
proposed_semantics: Keep AO and indirect-lighting requirements visible in the reference map.
Select bounded AO and/or an indirect-lighting model only when a production needs them; do not infer general GI from emission.

common: Conventional compute/raster or bounded probe/field techniques, to be chosen for the semantic.
optional: Ray-based AO or allowed nontraining GI implementations; no online-trained radiance cache.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Particles and spatial effects
current_scope: The existing History particle system stores x, y, vx, vy and age, steps at 120 Hz and bounces within image-space width/height bounds.
A generated compute path and CPU reference update exist.
limitations: The reviewed operator has no authored scene, camera or depth input; it is not a general world-space 3D emitter/renderer.
Lifetime/emitter/material parameter schemas alone must not be read as broader realized particle behavior than _step_particles/_history_hlsl implement.
proposed_semantics: World-space seeded emitters with position/velocity/lifetime, bounded emission, size/material and attachment to animated objects.
Render through scene cameras with depth-aware occlusion; use analytic evaluation or existing History reconstruction for transport changes.

common: Shared fixed-step scheduler and conventional compute plus raster/compute particle rendering.
optional: Work Graphs only if GPU work generation is useful; ray-based interaction only if separately needed.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Explicit temporal state and image feedback
current_scope: The shared History scheduler supplies previous-tick state externally, owns ping-pong resources and supports bounded replay/reset/checkpoints.
The current feedback implementation applies decay/gain and deterministic generated injection to prior image state.
limitations: Only the two listed built-ins expose History schemas.
The current feedback operator has no authored current-image input, scene depth or camera-cut metadata.
Artistic feedback is not equivalent to temporal denoising/reconstruction.
proposed_semantics: Feed actual current rendered images into reusable feedback/composition.
Define resets at camera cuts and time discontinuities; reuse the existing scheduler, lifetime and replay model.

common: Existing shared scheduler and compute passes.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Postprocessing and color response
current_scope: Bloom and tonemapping have concrete shader/export implementations; the History export path supports downstream image post passes.
limitations: The fixed 3D exporter requires exactly one half-resolution bloom followed by one tonemap.
The available post stack is not the full blur, distortion, depth-of-field, grading and stylization vocabulary.
DLSS/denoising does not replace intentional artistic post effects.
proposed_semantics: Reuse bloom and tonemapping in general image composition.
Add required filtering, grading and spatial/depth-driven effects as production needs emerge, preserving their authored visual purpose.

common: Conventional compute/raster image passes.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Procedural audio and audiovisual sequencing
current_scope: NWAS v1 is an actual bounded song payload, compiled separately from the visual operator graph and embedded in the optional audio package.
The reviewed synth generates mono PCM16 using integer triangle oscillators, fixed attack/release and saturating mixing; the song limit is 64 events.
limitations: No nw.audio.* operator IDs are implemented in the reviewed visual registry.
The current payload does not provide a multi-instrument/track/filter/automation graph or a Werkkzeug/V2 synthesizer replacement.
Existing event limits are current-version limits, not a proposed permanent design.
proposed_semantics: Compile bounded periodic/noise sources, authored envelopes, a stable bounded filter, gain/pan, music/effect sequencing and explicit instrument/voice budgets into the shared audio system.
Preserve NWAS v1 compatibility and the authoritative sample/timeline relationship.

common: CPU/offline-specialized synthesis and shared WASAPI/sample-clock integration.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Antialiasing, reconstruction and presentation enhancement
current_scope: No reusable image-reconstruction or vendor-inference operator was found in the reviewed registry and export paths.
limitations: The existing image pipeline does not by itself demonstrate the motion/depth/material/history inputs required by a selected reconstruction integration.
Frame generation does not create authored simulation ticks or replace camera/particle/audio sequencing.
An allowed pretrained model is a candidate backend, not evidence that its integration exists.
proposed_semantics: Backend-neutral image reconstruction/antialiasing with explicit resolution and history behavior.
Evaluate allowed vendor-supplied pretrained inference only after the chosen integration's required inputs are supplied; preserve the common path.

common: A conventional image reconstruction/antialiasing path appropriate to the selected production.
optional: DLSS Super Resolution/DLAA, Ray Reconstruction and frame-generation components may be evaluated separately, subject to actual capability/input requirements and no nodewerk-owned training.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.

families.title: Text, vector outlines and geometric paths
current_scope: No dedicated text, font, vector-outline or geometric-spline construction operator was found in the reviewed registry.
Scalar keyframe curves are present but do not establish geometric path/text functionality.
limitations: A glyph mesh, bitmap text, geometric path and scalar time curve have different output contracts.
No replacement or obsolescence is claimed merely because geometry can be represented as an implicit field.
proposed_semantics: Keep text/vector/path requirements in the reference inventory; select a bounded clean-room representation when a real production requires them.

common: Compiler-side/CPU geometry or bitmap generation; conventional rendering.

reference_query.status: Search hints only; not operator equivalence or reachable-demo usage.
